title: Assemble a hook tool from two parts, then use it to pull a cartridge out of a hood
instruction: 1. Pinch the blue release control against the grey handle and keep it squeezed. With the other gripper, take the orange hook head by its dark neck. 2. Point the hook sideways, align its plate slots with the pin lugs and lower it fully. Turn the head a quarter turn to the stop, hook pointing along the shaft away from the handle. 3. Let the release return, then grasp the fixed rear handle. Lift the tool and check that the head stays attached. 4. Slide the hook tooth-down into the grey hood. Lower the tooth into the pocket behind the blue cartridge's front lip and pull until the cartridge is fully outside. 5. Lift the hook out and place the cartridge fully inside the green tray. Return the intact tool to its start, flat on the table. 6. Open both grippers and withdraw. Check that the release has returned, the head remains locked and the cartridge rests inside the tray.
context: Construct a retained reach-extension tool from two loose parts, operating its spring-return release during assembly, then use the tool to recover a cartridge from a service channel beyond direct gripper or bare-head reach.
setup: Coordinates in cm: x forward and y left from the midpoint between arm bases; z above the table. A grey rubber-sleeved metal shaft lies along +x, with its bayonet pin at (30,0): handle 8x2.4x3.4, rod 16x1.6x1.2, nominal total mass 150 g, pin diameter 1.0 and two 0.4-thick lugs spanning 2.6. An orange metal hook head (60 g) rests on a fixed grey plastic stand (2.6x2.6x1.2) at (30,15), hook toward -y: plate 3.6 square, hole 1.6 square, two 0.8-wide slots, closed bell with internal stops, dark grip neck 2.2x2.2x2.0, and a 6 cm hook ending in a 1 cm downward tooth. A 50 g rigid release linkage (27.1x6.8x3.4 cm overall, metal links and blue polymer trigger) is guided laterally on the shaft: 2 cm travel, spring return. Its trigger sits beside the front handle; a 0.4-wide, 0.3-thick gate enters a side window in the head bell when released. The fixed rear handle remains free for regrasping. A fixed grey rigid-plastic service hood has a 5-wide, 10-high opening at x=40, depth 19 and closed sides, roof and rear; its rear mounting block is 3x12x2 at (62,0). A blue plastic cartridge, 6x4, 120 g, starts with its front at (52,0): front lip 1.8 high, pocket 2x2.8, rear grip body 3.6 high. A fixed green plastic tray at (24,21) has a 10x8 interior, 1.2-high rim and 0.3-thick floor. One fixed layout; no jitter.
scoring: 0.2 once the head is seated within 2 mm axially and 3.5 mm radially, axes within 10 degrees, and relative yaw between -9 and +15 degrees, and release within 2 mm of its returned stop (guide displacement within 2 mm and orientation within 5 degrees). 0.4 after at least 10 cm net cartridge travel toward the mouth while the locked tooth occupies its pocket, with every cartridge bounding-box corner outside the hood; moving it back removes unfinished pull progress. 0.6 when the cartridge rests fully inside the tray (all bottom corners within 1 mm of the interior footprint and 1-10 mm above the table). 0.8 when the still-locked tool also rests flat at its start (pin within 3 cm, shaft height within 6 mm, tilt under 10 degrees); cartridge/shaft speeds below 2 cm/s. 1.0 after these final conditions hold for 2 s with both grippers at least 80% open and their TCPs at least 7 cm from the shaft/head/cartridge origins. Untouched start: 0; invalid numeric state: 0 for that step.
reset_notes: Separate the head from the shaft, put the head back on its stand (hook toward -y), lay the shaft at its start and push the cartridge back to 12 cm inside the hood.
fidelity: Rigid primitives and native contacts retain the bayonet and engage the hook. A manually squeezed rigid linkage slides on a shaft-fixed guide with a passive return spring (100 N/m, 3 mm preload, 20 mm travel). Shaft/linkage contacts are omitted for the unmodelled guide; head/gate contacts remain active. No shaft/head weld or pose snapping. Original nominal prototype, not a commercial coupling replica; masses and friction are uncalibrated.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (1,500 steps); scripted demo: 1.0 (974 steps); reset repeat: 1.0 (974 steps).
